feedback.explanation: This test first failed in run 45 when the remove() method was initially implemented, producing assertion errors on return values. The test passed by run 51 after a 5-line removal and 1-line addition to BinarySearchTree.java. Run 54's major refactor (14 lines removed, 3 added) reintroduced the failure with wrong return values. Run 55's comprehensive rewrite (19 lines removed, 19 added) restored the correct return behavior. Across these runs, the return value contract was fragile—each time the method structure changed significantly, the return statement either was not updated or was placed incorrectly in the control flow.

feedback.pattern: Logic error in non-BST search requiring full tree traversal
feedback.explanation: This test was part of the initial batch and failed from run 1 due to a missing containsNonBST() method (compilation error). Run 2 resolved the compilation error for isEmpty(), and run 3 introduced the containsNonBST() implementation, which compiled but had a logic error: it returned false when the value was actually in the tree. Runs 4 and 5 showed no code changes. The breakthrough came in run 9 with a 20-line addition, which rewrote the method to perform a full tree traversal (e.g., checking both left and right subtrees recursively) instead of using BST properties. The method name indicates it should search the tree without assuming BST ordering, which requires visiting all nodes rather than pruning branches. The 8 failed runs and very low meaningfulness score reflect the time required to implement a full traversal approach.
nextSteps: Clarify the difference between contains() (which can use BST properties to prune the search) and containsNonBST() (which must check all nodes because the tree may not maintain BST ordering). Implement containsNonBST() as a full recursive traversal that checks the current node and then searches both left and right subtrees.

Test containsNonBST() on a tree that violates BST properties (e.g., a left child greater than its parent) to confirm it still finds values correctly. This will reinforce that the method cannot rely on ordering.
Consider whether containsNonBST() should be used for validation or testing purposes, and document this in a comment to avoid confusion with the standard contains() method in future work.

feedback.explanation: This test failed starting in run 45 with the initial remove() implementation, producing an assertion error indicating an incorrect tree size after removal (expected 3 but got 2). The error persisted through runs 46, 49, 51, and 52 despite multiple code changes. Run 51 recovered from a major regression but testRemoveAdvanced remained the only failing test, indicating the basic removal cases were fixed but the advanced case (likely removing a node with two children) was still broken. Run 52's attempted fix did not resolve the issue. The breakthrough came in run 55 with a comprehensive 19-line rewrite of the remove() method. The 7 failed runs and low meaningfulness score reflect a prolonged debugging cycle focused on a specific algorithmic challenge—likely in correctly identifying and removing the in-order successor or predecessor without losing nodes.
nextSteps: Focus on the two-child removal case: when removing a node with two children, you must find either the in-order successor (smallest value in the right subtree) or predecessor (largest value in the left subtree), remove it from its original position, and place it in the removed node's position. Trace through this logic step-by-step with a concrete example to ensure no nodes are lost.

Verify that after removing the successor/predecessor from its original location, the tree structure is still valid and the size is correctly decremented. A common mistake is forgetting to update the parent's pointer to the successor/predecessor's child.

Add a specific test case for removing a node with two children where both subtrees are non-trivial (e.g., the right subtree has a left child). This will help you catch edge cases in successor/predecessor removal that simpler cases might miss.
